dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a measure μ and a real-valued function X, LocalDef001 μ X is the real Bochner integral ∫ X(ω) dμ(ω).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The first equality unfolds this definition, and the same quantity is used as the centering constant inside LocalDef002.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given μ and X, LocalDef002 μ X is LocalDef001 applied to the function ω ↦ (X(ω) − LocalDef001 μ X)^2; equivalently, it is the integral of the squared deviation of X from its LocalDef001 value.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The second equality unfolds this definition into the integral of (X(ω) minus the integral of X)^2.

binders: {Ω : Type u}: An implicit type Ω in universe u, serving as the sample space.
[MeasurableSpace Ω]: An implicit measurable-space structure on Ω.
(μ : Measure Ω): An explicit measure μ on Ω.
[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]: An implicit proof/typeclass instance that μ is a probability measure.
(X : Ω → Real): An explicit real-valued function, interpreted as a random variable on Ω.
hypotheses: Measurable X: X is measurable from the given measurable space on Ω into the Borel measurable space on Real.
conclusions: LocalDef001 μ X = integral μ (fun ω => X ω): LocalDef001 of μ and X equals the real Bochner integral of X with respect to μ.

LocalDef002 μ X = integral μ (fun ω => (X ω - integral μ (fun x => X x))^2): LocalDef002 of μ and X equals the real Bochner integral of the square of X(ω) minus the real Bochner integral of X; the inner variable x is a bound dummy variable.
And of the two equalities: Both equalities are asserted together.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001: LocalDef001 μ X := ∫_Ω X(ω) dμ(ω).
LocalDef002: LocalDef002 μ X := LocalDef001 μ (ω ↦ (X(ω) − LocalDef001 μ X)^2) = ∫_Ω (X(ω) − ∫_Ω X(x) dμ(x))^2 dμ(ω).
Measurable X: For every Borel measurable subset B of Real, X⁻¹(B) is measurable in Ω.
Probability measure: μ is assumed to have the probability-measure property, including total mass μ(Ω) = 1.
Integral: Every occurrence of integral is the real-valued Bochner integral against μ.
Centered square: For each ω, subtract the integral of X from X(ω) using real subtraction and square the result using natural exponent 2.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every probability measure μ on Ω, and every Borel-measurable real-valued function X on Ω, LocalDef001 is exactly the integral of X, and LocalDef002 is exactly the integral of the squared difference between X and the integral of X.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The only explicit regularity assumption on X is measurability; there is no hypothesis that X is Bochner integrable, absolutely integrable, square-integrable, or has finite first or second moment.

Accordingly, the expressions are Lean's totalized Bochner integrals and should not automatically be read as asserting the usual finite expectation or finite variance of an arbitrary measurable random variable.
The proposition asserts definitional expansion of LocalDef001 and LocalDef002, not a substantive probabilistic theorem derived from the probability-measure or measurability assumptions.

The probability-measure assumption and the measurability hypothesis may be logically unnecessary for proving these equalities, because the local definitions and integral expressions can be unfolded without using them.

The conjunction is not vacuous in the logical sense, but it risks being mathematically weak: both conjuncts follow from the supplied local definitions rather than establishing existence, finiteness, or a new identity.
